title: Coextensive 10 m shared-phreatic storage-ownership oracle
purpose: Turn the original 10 m gravel-column thought experiment into an explicit physical-volume oracle for storage ownership when dummy-SWAP and MODFLOW are declared to represent the same phreatic storage volume.

correct_partition_sweep.expected: Every partition reproduces H=8.05 and the sum of owned storage-volume increments equals the one geometric physical volume increment 0.010 m3.

deliberate_duplicate_ownership.interpretation: Both components claim the same geometric 0.20 drainable storage.

gates: The analytical geometric volume law gives exactly 0.010 m3 for a rise from 8.00 to 8.05 m.
All five correct ownership partitions converge and reproduce 8.05 m within 1e-10 m.
For every correct partition, MODFLOW-owned gain plus SWAP-owned gain equals both the atmospheric input and geometric physical volume gain within 1e-12 m3.
The alpha=0 and alpha=1 endpoint controls both reproduce the same physical state.
The deliberate duplicate-ownership run converges to 8.025 m within 1e-10 m.
For duplicate ownership, numerical bookkeeping closes to 0.010 m3 while the single declared geometric volume changes by only 0.005 m3.
interpretation_rules: Storage coefficients alone do not determine whether two terms are duplicate; domain ownership does.
The same algebra can be valid for two distinct physical reservoirs and invalid for one coextensive physical reservoir.
In a true coextensive shared-phreatic contract, the sum of subsystem-owned storage responses must equal the one physical geometric storage response, with no overlap and no gap.
This test does not imply that current F-GC45 is duplicate-storage, because MAP11 established that F-GC45 does not declare coextensive phreatic storage.
forbidden: do not set production MODFLOW Sy/Ss to zero from this oracle alone
do not reinterpret finite-window real-SWAP u_A as a static Sy
do not apply the coextensive ownership conclusion to boundary-coupled distinct-domain configurations
